To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bacterial lysate BV is a potent macrophage activating agent.

(1) a bacterial extract (BV) is able to stimulate the oxidative metabolism and the cytolytic activity of mouse macrophages; (2) the effect of BV on the oxidative metabolism of macrophages is similar to that induced by bacterial endotoxins (LPS), whereas the cytotoxic effect is not; (3) BV is able to stimulate macrophage cytotoxicity in the absence of LPS, and the effect is not blocked by polymyxin B;
a bacterial extract (BV) can stimulate the metabolic and functional properties of murine macro phages, and that this effect can be further enhanced by the presence of MAF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stimulation by a bacterial extract of the metabolic and cytotoxic properties of murine macro phages.
the development of a new vaccine for the prevention of bronchitis.

the stimulation by a bacterial lysate (Broncho VAXOM) of the metabolic (glucose catabolism, O2 production) and functional activities (cytotoxicity against tumor cells, intracellular killing of Leishmania enr.) of murine macro-phages (peritoneal, bone-marrow derived).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BV is able to induce a significant stimulation of the metabolic and effector functions of macrophages in vitro.
BV is a safe immunopotentiating agent, which is able to stimulate the immune system in vitro as well as in vivo.
Broncho Vaxome (BV) is a bacterial lysate preparation that can stimulate the metabolic and functional capacities of macrophages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BV can be used as a macrophage activating agent, and that the mechanism of BV stimulation is distinct from LPS.
the stimulation by the bacterial lysate BV of macrophage activities is mediated by MAF and not by endotoxin.
the stimulation of the immune system by BV can be attributed to the presence in this preparation of a number of bacterial components, including LPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bacterial lysate BV is a potent stimulator of the metabolic and cytotoxic activities of macrophages, and that this activity does not depend on LPS contamination.
BV is able to induce the metabolic and functional activation of murine macro phages.
BV has a strong immunostimulatory activity on the macrophage system.
